title: M. abscessus as a rapid-growing hard NTM
dek: Wikipedia's abscessus page is a rapid grower with infamous drug recalcitrance. Not MTBC. Not a TB catalogue.
story: M. abscessus on Wikipedia is a rapid-growing NTM pack (abscessus/bolletii/massiliense in various splits) that causes lung disease in structural lung disease and horrible skin/soft-tissue outbreaks when devices are dirty.
It can grow in days on ordinary media, which is how it ambushes a lab expecting Mtb's calendar. It will not belong in a WHO TB mutation catalogue.
Inducible macrolide resistance (erm) folklore is NTM genetics, not katG. Do not paste TB DST logic here.
deep: CF and bronchiectasis clinics know this name; TB clinics should too when Xpert is negative and something grows fast.
Surgical device outbreaks are infection-control, not airborne TB wards by default — still assess the syndrome.
tb-ntm is the hand-off for not mis-filing the bottle.
No abscessus dosing on this card.
